newsitem.title: USA: Thermo King says faces sluggish market in '97.
newsitem.headline: Thermo King says faces sluggish market in '97.

text.p: A sluggish North American truck and trailer market this year could dampen profitability at Westinghouse Electric Corp's Thermo King subsidiary, said Jim Watson, Thermo King's president, on Tuesday.
"I'm not going to tell you there's not going to be any deterioration in margins," Watson told reporters at a press briefing at Thermo King's headquarters in Minneapolis.
Watson declined to give projections. Thermo King, a refrigerated transport unit that is part of Westinghouse's industrial group, had '96 revenues of $1 billion and operating profit of $186 million.
Watson said truck and trailer manufacturers were predicting a sluggish market this year. "I don't know that I can disagree with that," he said.
But he said there were growth opportunities this year for Thermo King in other areas, including container refrigeration, bus air conditioning and small truck refrigeration.
"There's a big, big opportunity in (small truck,) especially in developing countries," he said.
Watson said Thermo King cut costs last year by $42 million and he expected another $42 million in cost savings this year, achieved through buyer incentives rather than employment reductions.
